events.excerpt: This discussion is split across two posts because of the forum’s per-post character limit. This first post covers the core interface, growth, authority, and validity. The continuation below covers private presentations, one-time entitlements, recovery, the implementation example, and discussion questions. I am exploring an extension for soulbound credentials that accumulate verified experiences over time and allow those experiences to support different applications. The motivation is: Past activity scattered across different protocols should be reusable as evidence for future eligibility. A person may participate in governance, complete community tasks, provide liquidity, borrow and repay assets, or receive an educational qualification. These experiences can support future requirements such as membership upgrades, contributor access, professional eligibility, or admission to an event. The proposed design uses a persistent, non-transferable credential to maintain continuity across those experiences. Applications can discover its currently accepted state, identify the rules that authorized that state, and evaluate whether the supporting claims remain usable. For privacy-sensitive applications, a holder should be able to prove a requirement such as “I have at least two qualifying contributions and satisfy a balance threshold” without including their complete activity history or exact balance in the presentation. This is a pre-ERC discussion. The core interface and implementation profiles below are proposals for review. No audited implementation or benchmark results are claimed

events.excerpt: Australia’s government will consider creating a new criminal offense to punish AI companies which knowingly release harmful models. Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models
events.title: Australia may make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime

events.excerpt: Advocates for cloud-native software have long argued that their approach to development makes applications portable across different Kubernetes environments. But VMware argues that’s not happening across hybrid clouds, and has taken the lead in an effort to improve matters. That effort, the new Workload Conformance Working Group in the Kubernetes community, aims to establish a shared standard for how workloads run on Kubernetes. The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. The proposed solution? “A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.” Prashanth Shenoy, VP of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, told The Register that standard is needed in part because applications packaged to run in public clouds don’t always run well in hybrid clouds. That’s challenging for VMware, and other vendors of hybrid clouds like Nutanix and Red Hat, because they all sell tools to create and run a stack that users can deploy to both on-prem infrastructure and public clouds. VMware therefore thinks it will find support for an effort to ensure that cloud-native apps

events.excerpt: This proposal specifies the JSON document that tokenURI returns in ERC-721 and ERC-6909 and that uri returns in ERC-1155 . Most deployed tokens already use this format, but only part of it was ever specified. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 define name , description and image . Everything else wallets and marketplaces show ( animation_url , attributes and its display_type values, external_url , background_color ) comes from a page OpenSea published in 2018. Clients fill the gaps differently, so the same token renders differently from one app to the next. Draft: erc-8495.md ( ethereum/ERCs#2163 ) The draft covers: Every field and its type, every display_type value in use, and what clients do with values that don’t match, such as booleans, quoted numbers and dates in milliseconds. The URI schemes clients must resolve ( https , ipfs , ar , data ), the ones they may resolve ( ipns , and web3 from ERC-4804 ), and the ones they must never resolve. Fetching rules: ipfs:// URIs instead of gateway URLs, sandboxing HTML in animation_url , and keeping server-side fetches away from private addresses. How later proposals add fields without breaking older clients. The Rationale cites an October 2026 survey of 708 Ethereum and Base contracts. 113 of the 204 IPFS gateway URLs in it failed when fetched as written, and more contracts use text as a display_type than string . events.excerpt: Release Notes Node version 11.2.1 is a pre-release version of cardano-node that is not yet recommended for use on mainnet. It is a maintenance release on top of 11.2.0 . It updates to ouroboros-consensus 5.4, cardano-api 11.12 and cardano-cli 11.7, which together reduce the node's memory use around ledger snapshots, and it raises the protocol version the node advertises in block headers to 11.3. For the full set of 11.2 changes (the new cardano-config configuration format, gRPC over HTTP/2, the removal of node-to-client versions below NodeToClientV_23 , and more), see the 11.2.0 release notes . Highlights: Lower memory use. Writing a ledger snapshot no longer temporarily grows live memory by about the snapshot's size. The ChainDB also no longer keeps the genesis ledger state alive, which saves several hundred MiB on networks with a large genesis UTxO or delegation set. Faster snapshots while syncing. Until the node has first caught up, ledger snapshots are written as soon as they are requested. The randomised snapshot delay applies only after that. LSM is supported for block production. events.excerpt: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD. Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services. The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests. Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message. "You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one." By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted. "We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said . "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation." Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines.
events.title: Ransomware threat blares from Vanderbilt University computers during cyberattack

events.excerpt: Microsoft will enable access to Anthropic's Claude models by default for UK Copilot tenants next month, giving administrators a deadline to decide whether US-based processing fits their compliance requirements. From December 9, UK tenants whose administrators have not already chosen a setting will have Claude access enabled. Administrators can disable it, but leaving the setting untouched means opting in. In this instance, Anthropic operates as a Microsoft subprocessor , and Claude models are already on by default for most customers in the Windows giant's commercial cloud. The exceptions, notably, include the European Union, the European Free Trade Association, and the UK. However, UK tenants aren't in scope for Microsoft's EU Data Boundary - launched at the start of 2023 - and so Redmond is flipping the switch for the country. Anthropic processes the relevant data in the United States, Microsoft's documentation states . Administrators therefore have until December 9 to review whether that meets their organization's data-handling requirements and set access accordingly. Microsoft is also retiring the setting that restricts Claude access to Microsoft 365 alone. "This affirms Microsoft's commitment to offering choice between leading AI models while maintaining enterprise-grade security and compliance," the Redmond-based biz said. So long as you don't mind processing happening in the US. ®

events.excerpt: Posting a factual decode of recent ACLManager role activity on Aave V3 Ethereum, in the dated-report style already used in this category. Three RISK_ADMIN_ROLE grants since 2 September 2026: 2 Sep 2026, block 25891729 — granted to 0xbe28…7744 and 0x529e…F6c5 (two grants, same transaction) 30 Sep 2026, block 26089561 — granted to 0x6f48d9cdb8ee6e17c96b2d8aec128af426a295c1 The 30 Sep recipient is a verified contract named RiskSteward, 20,061 bytes of deployed code. All three grants were sent by 0x5300A1a15135EA4dc7aD5a167152C01EFc9b192A, which is the governance Executor. So these passed governance rather than originating from a standalone admin key — worth stating explicitly, since a RISK_ADMIN grant from an EOA would read very differently. Practical scope: RISK_ADMIN can change supply and borrow caps, LTVs, liquidation thresholds and reserve configuration without a full governance vote. Routing it through a RiskSteward contract constrains what the holder may change, which is the safer pattern, but each grant still widens the set of actors who can move risk parameters between votes. Context: the ARFC “Activate Aave Risk Stewards on Aave V4” thread is now closed with AIP #523 executed, so I’m posting this separately rather than reverting that thread. Method note: this is decoded from ACLManager’s RoleGranted logs plus the role constants read off the contract itself. I have not diffed storage layouts or reviewed the RiskSteward contract’s internal constraints — so I’m not making any claim about what that specific steward is or isn’t able to do.
